concepts.title: Meaning and Types of Business Services

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning and Types of Business Services' refers to.
questions.a: Business services are intangible activities that support the functioning of business but do not result in ownership of a physical product, and include services such as banking, insurance, transportation, warehousing and communication that facilitate business operations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning and Types of Business Services'.
questions.a: Services are intangible, inseparable, variable and perishable, and they differ from goods because they cannot be stored or owned as physical objects.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning and Types of Business Services' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Introduction to Business Services

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Banking Services' refers to.
questions.a: Banking services refer to the functions performed by banks which accept deposits from the public, lend money for productive purposes, and facilitate payments and other financial services, acting as financial intermediaries in the economy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Banking Services'.
questions.a: Banks are the backbone of the financial system, mobilising savings from depositors and channeling them as credit to borrowers, thereby supporting production, trade and economic growth.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Banking Services'.
questions.a: What are banking services and what is their role in the economy?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Bank Accounts' refers to.
questions.a: Types of bank accounts include savings account, current account, recurring deposit account and fixed deposit account, each designed to meet different needs of depositors regarding liquidity, interest and savings goals.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Bank Accounts'.
questions.a: Each account type offers a different balance between liquidity, interest earnings and deposit discipline, suited to different categories of customers such as individuals, businesses and savers.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Types of Bank Accounts'.
questions.a: Explain the different types of bank accounts available to customers.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Insurance: Life and General' refers to.
questions.a: Insurance is a contract between two parties whereby one party, the insurer, agrees to compensate the other party, the insured, for a financial loss caused by an uncertain event in exchange for a premium; it is broadly classified into life insurance and general insurance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Insurance: Life and General'.
questions.a: Life insurance provides protection against the risk of premature death and encourages savings, while general insurance covers risks to property, health, vehicles and other assets against fire, theft, marine and other perils.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Insurance: Life and General' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Insurance

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Principles of Insurance' refers to.
questions.a: The principles of insurance are the fundamental rules governing insurance contracts, including utmost good faith, insurable interest, indemnity, subrogation, contribution, proximate cause and mitigation of loss, which ensure fairness and prevent misuse of insurance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Principles of Insurance'.
questions.a: These principles ensure that insurance is used only to compensate for actual losses and not as a source of profit, maintaining the integrity and fairness of the insurance contract.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Principles of Insurance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Insurance

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Postal Services' refers to.
questions.a: Postal services are the communication services provided by the postal department that facilitate the movement and delivery of letters, parcels and money across the country, including mail services like inland letters, postcards, registered post and speed post, and financial services like money orders.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Postal Services'.
questions.a: The postal network is one of the largest and oldest communication systems in India, providing affordable and reliable mail and financial services even to remote rural areas.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Postal Services' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Communication Services

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Telecommunication Services' refers to.
questions.a: Telecommunication services are communication facilities that transmit information over distances through electronic means, including telephone services, mobile services, internet, fax and email, enabling rapid exchange of voice, data and written information.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Telecommunication Services'.
questions.a: Telecommunication services provide fast, reliable and long-distance communication essential for business coordination, information exchange and modern commercial operations.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Telecommunication Services' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Communication Services

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'E-Banking' refers to.
questions.a: E-banking or electronic banking is the delivery of banking services through electronic channels such as the internet, mobile phones and ATMs, allowing customers to access accounts, transfer funds, pay bills and conduct transactions without visiting a bank branch.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'E-Banking'.
questions.a: E-banking provides anytime, anywhere banking convenience through digital channels, reducing the need for physical branch visits and making transactions faster and more efficient.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'E-Banking'.
questions.a: What is e-banking and what are its advantages?
